questions.q: What happens when the router's first reply is chatty prose instead of JSON?
options: The tool crashes
Validation rejects it, the error is added to the prompt, and the retry can recover
The tool returns the prose to the user
The tool switches to the documents path
questions.explain: The validator returns an error, route() retries once with the rejection appended, and only gives up (with a safe message) if the retry also fails.

questions.q: The stubbed router returns a filter for a region called "Mars". Why does the tool reject it?
options: Filter values are checked against the real values in the table
Mars is a reserved word in pandas
Because the metric was revenue
Because JSON cannot hold planet names
questions.explain: validate_route checks each filter value against set(df[col]), so a value that does not exist in the data is rejected.

questions.q: In the data path, what role does the model's JSON play?
options: It is executed as Python code
It replaces the table
It selects keys (metric, grouping, filters) that are looked up in a whitelist, and pandas does the calculation
It is ignored
questions.explain: The model never supplies code to run. Its choices index into AGG and column filters, so numbers come from your own pandas code.

questions.q: Which parts of this build are stubbed rather than real?
options: Only the language model, which is a rule-based fake function
The pandas calculations
The TF-IDF retrieval
The validation logic
questions.explain: Retrieval, validation, and pandas are real code. Only the language model is replaced by a hand-written stub, which should be stated in any write-up.

questions.q: For a document question where no document scores above the retrieval threshold, what does ask() do?
options: Passes the whole document set to the model
Retries retrieval with a lower threshold automatically
Answers from the sales table instead
Returns "I don't know based on the available documents."
questions.explain: An empty hit list short-circuits to an honest I don't know rather than letting a model invent an answer.
